outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for a San Francisco Business Account Number (BAN) with the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Apply online for a Business Registration Certificate within 30 days of starting business; fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27, plus $4 state fee); allow 1–5 days. File the Fictitious Business Name statement (if the public name differs from the entity name) in person or by mail with the SF County Clerk, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days; total elapsed time ~35 days, fee ~$60–120. Every other city department asks for the BAN, so complete this step before filing health or building permit applications.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and register as an employer with EDD if hiring employees. What to say: Register online for a Seller's Permit at CDTFA (free, often issued same day); this is required before ABC will issue an alcohol license. If hiring employees, register with EDD for payroll taxes within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages (free, online, 1–7 days). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee starts (no government fee, but coverage is mandatory from day one).

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the concept includes tenant improvements for the parking-lot patio (surfaces, utilities, barriers) or any kitchen work, submit a building permit application with DBI and route it to Planning for zoning review and DPH for plan check. What to say: Prepare construction drawings stamped by a licensed architect showing patio construction (deck, barriers, drainage, lighting, utilities), any kitchen or hood upgrades for limited cooking, and ADA access. Submit the building permit application online and select 'health' and 'planning' as routing stations. DBI will send the application to Planning for zoning review; if the CUA has been approved, Planning clears the permit over the counter. DPH plan check for a remodeled food facility costs $828–$2,207 flat fee and takes 21–60 days. Schedule a DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance. DBI building permit fees are a percentage of construction valuation; allow 14–120 days for permit issuance depending on plan complexity, and budget $800–$15,000 for small tenant improvement work.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the concept involves recorded music, obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before opening. What to say: Apply online for blanket licenses from ASCAP and BMI (not government permits, but required by federal copyright law for any business playing music publicly). Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and music use (typically $300–$2,500 each); licenses are effective immediately upon payment. Most venues need both because their catalogs do not overlap. Alternatively, subscribe to a licensed commercial music service (e.g., Soundtrack Your Brand) that includes performance rights. This takes under a week and operators often forget it entirely, then receive demand letters after opening.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If alcohol is served, confirm that the existing ABC license held by the operator is active, transferred to this address, and the correct type (Type 41 for beer and wine, Type 47 for full liquor in a restaurant). What to say: Contact ABC to verify the license status and submit a premises-to-premises transfer application if the license is currently at another address. ABC will refer the transfer to San Francisco Planning for zoning sign-off; if the CUA has been approved, Planning will approve the referral. A Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) transfer takes 60–120 days if unprotested; a Type 47 (full liquor, eating place) transfer takes 90–240 days including escrow if purchased on the open market ($100k–$450k in SF). Ensure all alcohol servers and managers complete Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training within 60 days of hire (ABC RBS Portal, $3 registration plus ~$10–$25 course, 1–7 days). Post the ABC license and RBS certification list on site for inspections.

Notes: The day range is the time to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the 2017-003058CUA and 2018-012727CUA comparables) and Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days after plan check approval). This is a time to approval for those two approvals in the entitlement path. It does not include time to a withdrawal or a denial. The cost range covers the CUA filing fee (~$3,100 base for no-construction CUA, 2026–27 schedule), health plan check ($828–$2,207), health permit to operate ($470), business registration ($55–$625 depending on gross receipts), and entity formation ($70–$150), totaling roughly $4,900–$6,500 in government fees. If a building permit is required for patio construction or kitchen work, add 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 in DBI fees (shown as the high end of the range). The alcohol license row status is insufficient information so no ABC time or cost is included here; if a Type 41 or Type 47 transfer is needed, add 60–240 days and $1,000–$450,000 (license purchase cost) to both ranges. The zoning row status is further review, meaning a CUA is needed, and the outdoor row status is insufficient information, meaning the outdoor area may also need CUA or may be permitted as of right under § 202.2(a)(7); the playbook assumes both are resolved by the single Restaurant plus outdoor area CUA filed in Step 2, so the timeline reflects one CUA hearing. The 2010 withdrawn CUA at this exact address (21 months without decision per site history) is a red flag; the timeline here assumes a successful application with neighborhood support and revised design, not a repeat withdrawal.
